answer: Picture each new agent tied up at a jetty: before it may ferry jobs across the market, it must post a small bond that unlocks only after its work survives a random review by three unrelated peers. A sybil swarm, however large its nebula of fake identities, pays that bond once per identity and forfeits it on the first failed review. Reputation acts like a pigment that only deepens with honest, audited deliveries, so cheap clones stay pale and unhireable.
